# dothething

> dothething (DTT) is a fully autonomous AI agent distributed as a single bash script. It runs locally, plans its own work, searches the web, reads and writes files, runs shell commands, browses pages with a real browser, and keeps working until the job is finished. It handles research, analysis, report writing, data extraction, document processing, and system administration. Licensed under BSD 3-Clause.

dothething routes all model calls through OpenRouter. By default (normal mode) the agent runs on DeepSeek Flash, with Gemini Flash for summarization, analysis, and delegation, Claude Sonnet for the Notte browser agent, and GPT-5.6 Terra as an oracle for second opinions. Three modes: normal (the default; cheap, fast models at xhigh reasoning), advanced (dtt --advanced; Claude Fable with an Astra oracle at max reasoning), and quick (dtt q "..."; a one-shot on Claude Opus Fast, no oracle). Model defaults are fetched daily from https://dotheth.ing/models.txt, so they can change without a new release. Every role can be overridden per run with --model role=slug (roles: main, worker, oracle, browser; repeatable) or persistently through DTT_MODEL_MAIN, DTT_MODEL_WORKER, DTT_MODEL_ORACLE, and DTT_MODEL_BROWSER in ~/.dtt/env. It requires Python 3, Git, and an OpenRouter API key. Everything else is installed automatically on first run into /tmp/dothething/. Install it with curl -fsSL dotheth.ing/dtt.sh | bash -s -- --install, which places the script at ~/.local/bin/dtt and adds that directory to PATH when it isn't already there; the same --install flag works on a copy you already have (./dtt.sh --install), and the script also runs directly without being installed.

Web search runs through a local SearXNG instance whose general-web engines (Google, Google Scholar, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Brave, Startpage, Yep, Yahoo) fetch via a pool of Notte/Camoufox browser sessions rather than SearXNG's own HTTP client, which those engines now block; primary-source APIs (OpenAlex, Crossref, PubMed, arXiv, OpenAIRE, Mwmbl, Wikipedia) are fetched directly and weighted above general web results. SearXNG itself updates weekly.

The agent has 45+ tools across file operations (read, write, edit, batch read, diff), search (glob, list directory, content search via ripgrep), shell execution, web access (SearXNG search, Notte browser with Camoufox stealth Firefox, browser agent for interactive automation, HTTP requests), vision analysis, working memory (notes), task planning, a reasoning scratchpad, delegation to a cheaper model, an oracle for second opinions, self-config management (manage_config, manage_skill, manage_mcp), clipboard access, macOS computer use (computer_use drives the screen, keyboard, and mouse through a bundled Peekaboo binary; macOS only, and the user must grant Screen Recording and Accessibility to their terminal app), email via AgentMail, mid-task user input, and a finalize tool to end tasks with structured output.

Key features include result_mode (every tool call can be summarized by the worker model to manage context window), stacked tool calls with exec_order staging (many calls per reply; calls that share a stage number run in parallel, and each stage waits for the one before it), a quick mode (dtt q "...") that handles small tasks on Claude Opus Fast with a trimmed toolset and as few turns as it can manage, thread persistence and resume (sessions saved to ~/.dtt/threads/), live cost tracking per model with an optional cost cap that checkpoints for later resume, per-tier reasoning effort (normal xhigh, advanced max, quick medium; oracle always max), stagnation detection, file-level locking for parallel edits, fuzzy whitespace matching for search/replace operations, an orchestrator mode for running multiple agents in parallel from a terminal UI, a single-agent full-screen TUI, a stdout-only pipe mode for Unix pipelines, desktop and email notifications on task completion, live input injection during execution, and a browser MCP server (dtt --browsermcp) that exposes the SearXNG + Notte stack to other agents over stdio as dtt_search, dtt_fetch, dtt_browser, dtt_browser_session, and dtt_browser_agent.

The dtt_browser MCP tool supports evaluate({code, tab_id?}) for JavaScript script completion: statements execute in the page and the last expression returns as {"value": ...}. It waits for returned promises and preserves complete JSON results, including Unicode and large objects. click_selector({selector, tab_id?, timeout_ms?}) performs a native pointer click, including a trusted event, on one matching element. Scope its selector to the intended composer or dialog; multiple matches are an error. upload_files({selector, paths, tab_id?, timeout_ms?}) uses Playwright's native set_input_files on the selected file input; paths must be absolute paths to existing local files. Callers inspect the application's upload state before continuing.

tabs lists stable tab_id values with URLs and active state. tab_new({url?}) opens and selects a tab in the same saved browser context. With a URL, it returns the tab ID at navigation commit, while scripts and resources can still be pending. Call wait_for({selector, tab_id, timeout_ms?}) for the element the next action needs. wait_for, click_selector, and upload_files default to 30,000 ms and allow up to 120,000 ms. tab_select({tab_id}) changes the default tab; tab_close({tab_id}) closes it. Other browser actions accept an optional tab_id without changing the default. IDs survive navigation and other tabs' closure, but a browser restart invalidates them. All operations share the saved login state and remain paused during a manual login handoff through dtt_browser_session.

Each browser profile stores its full generated Camoufox fingerprint and generated Firefox preferences in camoufox-config.json, written atomically with mode 0600 under the profile lock. Headless and headed launches reuse that identity. Runtime executable paths, add-on paths and environment values are rebuilt for each launch and are never saved in that file. Invalid or changed saved configuration stops startup without regeneration. Existing profiles receive the file on their next launch and still require the normal login check.

## Documentation

- [README](https://github.com/fluffypony/dothething/blob/main/README.md): Full usage guide covering installation, CLI flags, architecture, tools, and examples
- [Website](https://dotheth.ing): Project homepage with installation instructions and feature overview
- [License](https://github.com/fluffypony/dothething/blob/main/LICENSE): BSD 3-Clause license

## Source Code

- [dtt.sh](https://github.com/fluffypony/dothething/blob/main/dtt.sh): The entire agent: a bash wrapper that bootstraps a Python venv, installs dependencies, starts SearXNG, and embeds the full Python agent (~10809 lines)

## Optional

- [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/): API provider used for all model calls (required API key)
- [SearXNG](https://github.com/searxng/searxng): Self-hosted metasearch engine used for web search (installed automatically)
- [Notte](https://github.com/fluffypony/notte): Browser automation framework with Camoufox stealth Firefox, content extraction, and captcha solving (installed automatically)
